liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help On The Way** (1 review): Opens a little loose, understandably since the material was new, before the band tightens up [13]
- **Slipknot** (1 review): By Slipknot! the band pulls together and jams extensively from there [13]
- **It Must Have Been The Roses** (1 review): Confirms the note that song order after Roses is wrong in the track listing and took time to work out [8]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Reviewer's all-time favorite is the Crazy Fingers into Drums segment [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Stronger Than Dirt**: rare: 10 archived performances [16]
- **Sage And Spirit**: rare: 3 archived performances [16]
- **Blues For Allah**: rare: 7 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd75-08-13.fm.vernon.23661.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 122 min; rated 4.85/5 by 67 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the quality excellent; Raw-feeling, somewhat flatter than the Vault release, with Phil sounding wonderful in the mix; Crisp FM sound with Phil mixed nicely; reviewer finds it stands up beside the official CD release [5][7][11][15]
- **gd1975-08-13.fm.cousinit.18512.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 120 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1975-08-13.155570.FM.flegel.flac1644**: FM broadcast; 17 songs; 123 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [3]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Bill Graham [1]
- The concert closes with Blues for Allah [5]
- Reviewer says the venue has energy across the dance floor and balcony; Phil has played there, jamming Franklin's Tower with Umphrey's McGee [12]
- Donated for the Music Never Stopped Project in 2003 [2]
- Reviewer says the remastered, remixed official Vault release is preferable to downloading this FM copy [6]
- Considers One from the Vault the ultimate copy, with this FM version a complement to it [7]
- Reviewer previously owned only a hissy analog copy; the official CD sounds perfect, and this FM rivals it [11]
- Reviewer likens the show to a Blues For Allah album plus extra songs [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd75-08-13.fm.vernon.23661.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard - FM [1]. Also: Track numbering is off: Roses and Eyes of the World share disc 1 track 6, so later tracks shift by one; Reviewer's copy came from a board tape recorded to 16-track Ampex, later made digital; Pitch-corrected version of the FM broadcast originally seeded by CousinIt, by Matt Vernon [1][5][15]
- **gd1975-08-13.fm.cousinit.18512.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by C>SHN Conversions by Cousinit; source: FM Source: SBD>FM>MC>DAT>WAV>SHN SBD Source: MSR>R(2)>C>DAT>WAV>SHN [2]. Also: FM broadcast aired 9/1/75 on the Metromedia Network; soundboard portion normalized in SoundForge to match FM levels [2]
- **gd1975-08-13.155570.FM.flegel.flac1644**: taped by Brian Flegel; transferred by Brian Flegel; source: (Bootleg Tape - from FM broadcast - 9/1/75) [3]. Also: Roses and a section of King Solomon's Marbles were patched in from the Make Believe Ballroom bootleg LP [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by lostlivedead.blogspot.com: [August 13, 1975: Great American Music Hall, 859 O'Farrell Street, San Francisco, CA (FM IX)](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2014/08/august-13-1975-great-american-music.html) [17]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Great American Music Hall - August 13, 1975](https://www.dead.net/show/august-13-1975) [18]
- Poster by lostlivedead.blogspot.com: [August 13, 1975: Great American Music Hall, 859 O'Farrell Street, San Francisco, CA (FM IX)](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2014/08/august-13-1975-great-american-music.html) [19]
